item.text:
Web-only note. I treated pre-2024 scandal origins and approval erosion as background; the items below separate 2024 actions/outcomes from agenda-setting context.

Question-ID mapping below is intentionally conservative and broad: `8B.*` for governing effectiveness, public-trust repair, and leadership performance.

**2024 Event Evidence**
- **[Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html)** — Prime Minister's Office of Japan, June 21, 2024. Status: 2024 event. Summary: Kishida said restoring trust in politics was the main Diet-session issue, highlighted that he had disbanded his faction, pointed to amendments to political-funds rules, and said 61 of 62 government bills passed, including child-support and agricultural legislation. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
- **[Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida regarding His Attendance at the NATO Summit and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/11kaiken.html)** — Prime Minister's Office of Japan, July 11, 2024. Status: 2024 event. Summary: Kishida reported concrete Japan-NATO cooperation outcomes, including stronger classified-information sharing, cyber and space cooperation, and continued support for Ukraine. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
- **[Japan's Prime Minister Kishida to resign, paving way for new leader](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455)** — Reuters, August 14, 2024. Status: 2024 event. Summary: Reuters reported Kishida would step down, framing the move as a response to public disaffection over political scandals and rising living costs; Kishida said the clearest first step to show the LDP was changing was for him to step aside. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
- **[August Opinion Polls Find Low Popularity for Kishida As He Ends His Term](https://www.nippon.com/en/japan-data/h30004/)** — Nippon.com, August 30, 2024. Status: 2024 event / contemporaneous measurement. Summary: Major August polls kept Kishida below 30% approval, with Jiji at 19.4% and NHK at 25%; respondents generally judged his decision to step down appropriate. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
- **[Statement by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio upon the General Resignation of the Kishida Cabinet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202410/1001danwa.html)** — Prime Minister's Office of Japan, October 1, 2024. Status: 2024 event. Summary: Kishida said the cabinet resigned en masse, portrayed his term as one of economic revival and defense strengthening, but acknowledged political fundraising issues had undermined trust. Question IDs: `8B.*`.

**Background / Agenda-Setting in 2024**
- **[Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html)** — Prime Minister's Office of Japan, January 30, 2024. Status: background / agenda-setting. Summary: Kishida apologized over the LDP funding scandal, launched the Political Reform Headquarters, and promised transparency and legal reforms while also tying 2024 to wage growth, child support, and economic revitalization. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
- **[Japan's Kishida championed 'new capitalism' but was undone by yen](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SONY-GROUP-CORPORATION-6492482/news/Japan-s-Kishida-championed-new-capitalism-but-was-undone-by-yen-47649114/) ** — Reuters, August 14, 2024. Status: background / retrospective assessment. Summary: Reuters said Kishida had pushed through some of Japan’s biggest wage increases in decades, but the weak yen, higher prices, and scandals outweighed that progress politically. Question IDs: `8B.*`.
